title: Making Parliament a Fairer Arena for All
what_it_is: Making Parliament a Fairer Arena for All

sections.label: MP assistant allowances
sections.summary: Elected MPs receive a monthly allowance of $1,300 for a Legislative Assistant and $500 for a Secretarial Assistant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In place of that, elected MPs are provided a monthly allowance of $1,300 to hire a Legislative Assistant and $500 for a Secretarial Assistant to assist them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I am sure most Members would agree with me that this is meagre and is completely insufficient to hire even one full-time assistant.

sections.label: NCMP and NMP allowances
sections.summary: NCMPs and NMPs do not receive such allowances, with Mr Wong Kan Seng citing lighter duties of NCMPs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Non-Constituency MPs (NCMPs) and Nominated MPs (NMPs) do not receive such an allowance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Then Leader of the House, Mr Wong Kan Seng’s justification for the removal of the NCMPs’ support allowances were that the duties of NCMPs were not as heavy and onerous as those of elected MPs, as only elected MPs sit on committees.

sections.label: Parliamentary research department
sections.summary: A department with a Head and full-time staffers should provide research support, with a starting budget of around $1 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This department should have a Head and several full-time staffers to provide research support for MPs as they scrutinise Bills and policies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I think an appropriate annual starting budget for such a department is around $1 million.

sections.label: Government data provision
sections.summary: The Government is to provide all data requested by Members in the requested format, unless national security or financial market sensitivity applies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Three, the Government is to provide all data requested by Members in the requested format unless there are national security or financial market sensitivity considerations.

sections.label: Question and clarification time
sections.summary: Question and answer and clarification time for all debates should not end while new substantive questions from MPs remain.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Two, in principle, the question and answer, and clarification time for all debates, including Parliamentary Questions (PQs), Ministerial Statements, Bills and Motions in this House should not end as long as there are new substantive questions from MPs.

sections.label: Public Accounts Committee chair
sections.summary: The Public Accounts Committee should be chaired by an Opposition Member, with all political parties represented.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: One, the Public Accounts Committee (PAC) should be chaired by an Opposition Member, with Members from all political parties represented on the Committee.

sections.label: Public Petitions Committee chairmanship
sections.summary: The Public Petitions Committee should also be chaired by an Opposition Member.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Two, the Public Petitions Committee (PPC) should also be chaired by an Opposition Member.

sections.label: NCMP voting rights and workload
sections.summary: NCMPs have the same voting rights as MPs but a lighter workload, lacking constituency and Meet-the-People Session duties.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: On the first point, NCMPs have the same voting rights as MPs in Parliament, but it is indisputable that their workload is less than that of elected MPs, as they do not have the responsibility for a specific constituency or for dealing with Meet-the-People Session (MPS) cases of residents.

sections.label: Resources for Leader of the Opposition
sections.summary: More resources were allocated to the Leader of the Opposition given greater Opposition presence and his expanded duties.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: In the case of the LO, having regard to the greater Opposition presence in Parliament after the last General Election and the designation of Mr Singh as "Leader of the Opposition" for this Parliament, it was appropriate to allocate more resources to him, given his expanded duties and responsibilities.

sections.label: Data provision costs for PQs
sections.summary: Over 7,000 PQs were filed, and collating and checking data in different formats costs time, money and effort.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: During the last session of Parliament, more than 7,000 PQs were filed and most answers would have involved the provision of data in some form or another.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Mr Leong says the Government must provide data in whatever format MPs want.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: I ask Mr Leong and Members to bear in mind that data collation, as well as slicing and dicing it in different ways and the need to check the data thereafter, costs time, money and effort.

sections.label: Time for Budget and Bills
sections.summary: MPs have about a month to study Bills, and the Budget Statement comes at least a week before debate.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The Budget Statement is delivered at least a week before the Budget debate and COS, so, MPs have ample opportunity to think through their speeches and cuts.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Bills are introduced during prior Sittings, except in cases of urgency, which are rare.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Hence, in general, MPs have about a month to go through the Bill, which forms the basis of the Minister's Second Reading speech.

sections.label: No need for Opposition hour
sections.summary: For this same reason, there is no need to have an Opposition hour.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: For this same reason, there is no need to have an "Opposition hour".

sections.label: UK Parliament Question Time
sections.summary: In the UK Parliament, Question Time lasts only one hour per Sitting day, including Prime Minister's Questions, with 650 MPs.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: In fact, in the UK Parliament, Question Time is only one hour per Sitting day, inclusive of Prime Minister's Questions and they have 650 MPs!

sections.label: Debate concludes and House adjourns
sections.summary: The debate concludes after 30 minutes under Standing Order 2(8)(b), and the House is adjourned, with the next Sitting at 11.00 am.

sentences.speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
sentences.text: Mr Leong, I am afraid that pursuant to Standing Order 2(8)(b), the debate concludes after 30 minutes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
sentences.text: You had 20 minutes for your speech and the Minister replied, using up the full 30-minute complement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
sentences.text: I adjourn the House pursuant to the Standing Order.

sentences.speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
sentences.text: I wish to inform hon Members that the Sitting tomorrow will commence at 11.00 am.
